newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain approves Retevision creation ahead of sale.
newsitem.headline: Spain approves Retevision creation ahead of sale.

text.p: Spain's cabinet approved the creation of Retevision as a second telephone operator on Thursday, in a formal move ahead of its privatisation.
"Retevision SA has been formed with a share capital of 40 billion pesetas," government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told journalists after the cabinet meeting.
The new firm will has a new worth of 64.1 billion pesetas and property worth 81.2 billion pesetas in technical centres, infrastructure and equipment as well as financial investments.
Retevision, which was a state television broadcaster, has been set up to be Spain's second basic telecommunications operator after Telefonica de Espana.
It has more than 1,800 technical centres spread throughout Spain, linked by a wide-band digital network of more than 18,000 km and covering 98 percent of the population.
The cabinet said in a statement that at least 51 percent of Retevision's share capital would be sold to a qualified bidder once the company was formally created.
The 1,200 workers at the broadcaster will be transferred to the new company, which has started to offer basic telephone services and all types of telecommunications.
